fieldMarks: Smaller than the willow ptarmigan with a smaller bill.
Winter: both sexes mostly white; winter male has a black line from bill to eye.
Breeding: females turn mottled brown before males; males stay mostly white into early summer.
behavior: Courting males give a snoring kurr-kurr.
Picks at vegetation: willow, dwarf birch, alder, saxifrage, crowberry buds, seeds and berries.
In winter sometimes follows caribou or muskox to feed where they scraped away snow.
Leaves the northernmost range and highest mountains in winter, moving lower and south in flocks.
habitat: Dry, open tundra with rock outcrops and dwarf shrubs, above timberline in mountains and on northern coasts.
range: Arctic and alpine tundra of Alaska and northern Canada.

lookalikes.name: Willow ptarmigan
lookalikes.howToTell: Willow is larger with a heavier bill; the winter male lacks the black eye line and breeding molt timing differs.
